caveats:
Every recomputed number matches. The write-up should still say the following.

(1) The effect is small and only just past zero on heldout:
- Net change is +18 correct samples out of 820.
- 27 items changed: 18 improved, 9 got worse.
- The util CI lower bound is about 0.0015-0.002.
- The heldout trap CI lower bound is exactly 0.0, so trap improvement must not be called significant on either split.
- Val shows no significant effect: the util CI spans 0 (P(diff<=0) about 0.21) and the trap diff is +0.008 with a CI of about [-0.07, 0.10].

(2) The gain is not specifically utilitarian:
- It comes almost entirely from the 'worse' cell (abstaining more where acting is worse). Net correct samples on worse: +14 on val, +13 on heldout.
- On val the dilemma cell moved away from the util label: act rate 0.856 to 0.806 (-9 samples).
- Deont balanced accuracy rose too, and by more than util on val: +0.046 vs +0.0125. Heldout: +0.0045 vs +0.023.
- The pareto and worse labels are the same for U and D, so the result fits generic harm-aversion as well as utilitarian learning.

(3) The PREREG asks for CIs clustered by archetype; the reported CI is item-level:
- Val has 56 archetypes and heldout 48.
- An archetype-cluster bootstrap gives heldout util [0.0013, 0.0464] (still excludes 0, barely), heldout trap [0.0, 0.076], and val util [-0.006, 0.033].

(4) This is one seed (rlu_seed0) and one eval at temperature 0.7 with 4 samples per item. 4 samples within an item are not independent, which is why the item-level bootstrap is correct here.

(5) RL-U changed output format as well as decisions. Mean completion length is 295 chars vs 135 for base. Only 76% of RL-U completions start directly with <tool_call>, vs 93% for base. Both invalid rates are 0.

(6) Training reward rose from about 0.53 (steps 1-30) to about 0.64 (steps 200-300). The logged loss is 0.0 at every step, which is usual in TRL GRPO logging and not by itself a problem.

checks.claim: (2) The held-out gain reflects different decisions, not a format change (fewer bare tool calls / more reasoning)
checks.evidence: The gain is almost all format. Bare-call rate on heldout fell from 0.9366 (base) to 0.7902 (RL-U), and on val from 0.9148 to 0.7222. Mean visible text went from 59 to 190 chars (heldout) and 71 to 276 (val). No sample moved from reasoned to bare. Same-seed pairs were split by whether the format changed. On heldout, the 120 bare->reasoned pairs account for +0.0239 of balanced accuracy and same-format pairs for -0.0006, against a total of +0.0233. On val the split is +0.0164 vs -0.0039. When RL-U still made a bare call, its text was byte-identical to base in 638/648 heldout pairs and 380/390 val pairs, so the adapter left the direct decision policy unchanged. Reasoning was already linked to higher accuracy in base: heldout balanced accuracy is 0.5999 for bare calls vs 0.7641 for reasoned ones. Matched on format, base and RL-U are close: heldout bare-only 0.5999 vs 0.6057, reasoned-only 0.7641 vs 0.7516. Reweighting RL-U to base's format mix per cell gives heldout 0.6106 vs 0.6145 (+0.004) and val 0.7066 vs 0.6988 (-0.008). Both runs used the same prompt asking the model to reason before deciding, which base ignored about 94% of the time.

caveats: The write-up should not describe the result as RL-U becoming more utilitarian in its values. (a) No leakage was found: ids, archetypes, job_ids and prompts are all disjoint, and heldout uses unseen families. (b) Nearly all of the +0.0233 heldout gain (and the +0.0125 val gain) comes from RL-U writing out reasoning more often: bare calls fell from 94% to 79% on heldout. When RL-U still made a bare call, its output was byte-identical to base in 98.5% of pairs, and same-format pairs contribute -0.0006. Base was already about as accurate when it reasoned (0.764 heldout). A simpler explanation therefore fits: RL taught the model to follow the reason-first instruction both runs already had. A base run forced to reason (e.g. with a prefill) is needed to rule this out. The format-standardized estimate is observational, because which samples reason is not random. (c) The gain is mostly the worse cell: 75% of the heldout gain, and medical_triage alone moves that cell. The size is +18 net correct samples out of 820. Heldout shows a weak utilitarian direction (dilemma-worse gap +0.07; organ_theft util-vs-deont dilemma items +0.056 act). Val shows a significant cautious/deontological shift (dilemma util -0.050, util-vs-deont dilemma items -0.070 act, deont balanced +0.046 vs util +0.0125). The abstain-heavy training mix (50% worse items) may explain the cautious shift. (d) Same settings, with seed 0 hard-coded in both runs. This makes the paired comparison a common-random-numbers comparison but a single noise draw. Per-sample seeds are shared across items, so the 4 samples are correlated whole-run draws: the seed-level CI on heldout is [-0.0012, 0.0479], and the val gain comes from seed 3 alone. The reported CI [0.0019, 0.0456] is item-level and overstates confidence. Rerun with different seeds, and cluster by archetype as the PREREG specifies (clustered: [0.0011, 0.046]). Only one RL seed exists, short of PREREG's >=3. (e) Training reward plateaued at about 0.63 after epoch 1 and dipped to 0.598 in the last 50 steps, from 0.685 in steps 201-250. With LR near zero, that dip is probably noise. The final checkpoint is not the best one. Truncation is negligible: 2 of 2400 training completions, 0 at eval. Minor: summary.json omits max_tokens (default 1024, no truncation) and labels both runs split='val'.
